subject: Aurora Labs — Capacity run-rate and accelerated commit proposal
messages:
From: Samantha Price <samantha@auroralabs.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@auroralabs.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity run-rate check

Jordan —

Quick check-in from our side as we head into next quarter. We ran a Q2 postmortem on model utilization and wanted to share a short summary and a couple of asks: 

- Average token consumption (chat + embeddings): ~32M tokens/month, with a sustained upward trend after March.
- Peak growth window: week of 6/12 — 48M tokens (mostly inference at 512–1024 context).
- Performance: 95th p95 latency on our Redwood endpoints drifted from ~180ms to ~260ms during spikes.

Attached is the CSV export from our internal billing and the sample trace snapshots. We are considering pulling forward additional committed capacity to stabilize latency and lower unit cost. Can Redwood provide a short proposal for a 2x committed baseline (24 -> 48M) with pricing and expected latency improvements?

Also worth calling out: we have an internal milestone for an enterprise feature launch on Sept 28 — any SLA guarantees around latency would be helpful to justify the commit.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Price
Head of Platform
Aurora Labs

[Attachment: aurora_usage_report_q2.csv]
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Price <samantha@auroralabs.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity run-rate check

Samantha — thanks for the export and the heads-up on the Sept 28 launch. We dug into Aurora's token mix and have a few recommendations and a fast proposal below: 

1) Capacity recommendation: move to a 2x committed baseline (nominally 48M tokens/month committed) with an additional burst pool for +25% traffic spikes. That should keep p95 under 200–220ms based on our current kernel selection and batching profiles.

2) Economics: current on-demand blended cost ~ $4.20 /M tokens for your mix. With a 12-month accelerated commit at 48M/mo we can offer an effective unit price of $2.85 /M tokens (applied as billing credits across months) + a one-time onboarding credit to offset migration smoothing.

3) Ops: we can enable prefix/KV caching on heavy conversational flows and a short-term quantization profile (8-bit where safe) to lower burst latency. Internal deployment plan takes ~7 business days after signature for Dedicated pool sizing and ~48 hours for routing cutover.

I've attached a short proposal PDF with the pricing and an uplift ROI calc that shows ~35% cost savings vs. your current run rate and a projected end-to-end latency improvement. If that looks reasonable, next steps are:

- Ben to confirm seat/ops pricing and finalize SLA addendum.
- Karthik to prepare billing schedule and DocuSign.
- Jordan/CS to schedule a technical runbook call (30m) for the week of Aug 23.

If you want, I can put together a small A/B test window (two-week pilot) at a reduced commit to validate latency numbers before a full 12-month acceleration.

Next steps: are you available for a 20–30 minute call on Wed 8/18 or Thu 8/19?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood-proposal-AUR-2027.pdf]
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Re: Capacity run-rate check

Looping in pricing to lock numbers. Jordan — quick notes from my side after reviewing the usage CSV and the proposal: 

- Confirming a 12-month accelerated commit at 48M/mo with a ramp credit equal to 10% of the first 3 months' spend.
- SLA addendum: target p95 latency <= 220ms with a 99.5% uptime target for the Dedicated pool. Exceptions for force majeure; standard credit schedule in the addendum.
- Billing cadence: monthly invoicing with a quarterly true-up.

Karthik — can you draft the billing schedule and generate the DocuSign envelope for the AUR-2027-42 deal? Include the ramp credit as a line item.

Soojin — please confirm capacity sizing for a 2x baseline + 25% burst pool and estimated lead time for GPU procurement (if any).

Ben
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Jordan / Ben —

Thanks — the numbers look good and the SLA target covers our launch needs. Procurement has confirmed budget approval pending the finalized DocuSign package. We are ready to proceed with the 12-month accelerated commit at 48M/mo. 

Please send the DocuSign link and we will review internally; we aim to return a signed copy by the end of this week so engineering can start the cutover work. Also, please include the 30-minute runbook call with our platform team (I'll add a calendar invite after I have the DocuSign).

Samantha
Head of Platform, Aurora Labs
